title: 金がないと自由になれない  (Without Money, You Cannot Be Free)

segments.t: Alone in his quiet house, Muranishi remembers post-war Fukushima when he was a boy. His mother Kozue discovers his father Konosuke spent the money meant to buy rice for young Toru—and later that night, Konosuke whispers a bitter lesson about money and freedom. Listen to this childhood memory.
仕事に戻って稼いでくればいいだろう！
黙ってろ！
あんた、まさか。
あれはとおるに米を食べさせるお金だったのに！
うるさい！
やめろ！
お前、何をやってるんだ！
ごめんなさい、ごめんなさい。
父ちゃん。
父ちゃん、ごめんな。許してくれ。
結局、金がないと自由にもなれないんだな。
金と自由か。
Even in these raw childhood memories, the everyday words are short and direct. Let's look at each one.
仕事に戻って稼いでくればいいだろう！
'You should go back to work and earn money!' "Modotte" comes from "modoru", to return, and "kasegu" means to earn a living.
黙ってろ！
'Keep quiet!' "Damattero" crushes "damatte iro", stay silent, into a harsh, clipped command from "damaru", to shut one's mouth.
あんた、まさか。
'Wait—surely you did not.' Whenever a dreadful suspicion hits you, "masaka" gasps 'no way—don't tell me...!'
あれはとおるに米を食べさせるお金だったのに！
'That was the money to feed rice to Toru!' Uncooked rice is "kome" (cooked rice in a bowl is "gohan"). "Tabesaseru" turns "taberu", to eat, into 'let him eat' or 'feed him'.
ごめんなさい、ごめんなさい。
'I am sorry, I am so sorry.' Here is full, heartfelt "gomennasai", more personal and emotional within a family than businesslike "sumimasen".
父ちゃん。
'Dad.' Rustic, affectionate "touchan" is like 'Dad'—warmer and rougher than textbook "otousan".
許してくれ。
'Please forgive me.' "Yurusu" means to forgive or pardon, and plain "yurushite kure" begs a family member for forgiveness.
結局、金がないと自由にもなれないんだな。

'In the end, without money you cannot even become free.' "Kekkyoku" sums things up with 'in the end' or 'after all'. Then "kane ga nai to", without money, leads into "jiyuu ni mo narenai", 'cannot even become free'.
金と自由か。

'Money and freedom, huh.' Linking two big ideas with "to"—"kane", money, and "jiyuu", freedom—and ending on musing "ka" shows Muranishi turning his father's words over in his mind. Now let's hear the Fukushima flashback again.
仕事に戻って稼いでくればいいだろう！
黙ってろ！
あんた、まさか。
あれはとおるに米を食べさせるお金だったのに！
うるさい！
やめろ！
お前、何をやってるんだ！
ごめんなさい、ごめんなさい。
父ちゃん。
父ちゃん、ごめんな。許してくれ。
結局、金がないと自由にもなれないんだな。
金と自由か。

Remember "masaka" for 'surely not!', "gomennasai" for heartfelt apologies, and "kekkyoku" when summing up what something comes down to in the end. Next, Muranishi wanders into Sapporo's Susukino night district.
また会いましょう。
